item.title: Restorative Justice Association of British Columbia
item.description: An applicant requested information from Restorative Justice Association of British Columbia (Association) under the Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA). The Association requested a time extension to respond to the request and declined to provide some of the requested information. The applicant claims that the Association did not provide a response within the time frame required by PIPA. The Adjudicator found that the Association failed to meet its obligations under s. 29(1) (time limit for response) and ordered the Association to respond to the applicant’s request within two weeks, in compliance with the requirements of ss. 28 (duty to assist individual) and 30(1) (content of response) of PIPA.

item.title: City of Powell River
item.description: Under the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act (FIPPA), an individual (the Applicant) requested the City of Powell River (City) provide access to records related to a fire department hiring process. The Applicant requested the Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner (OIPC) review the City’s decision to refuse access. The matter was eventually forwarded to the OIPC’s inquiry phase for adjudication. At the inquiry, the adjudicator found s. 3(3)(h) (question or answer to be used on an examination or test) did not apply; therefore, the relevant records were subject to FIPPA. The adjudicator also determined the City was not authorized to refuse access to the information at issue in those records under s. 13(1) (advice or recommendations), but it was required to refuse access to some information in other records under s. 22(1) (unreasonable invasion of third-party personal privacy). The adjudicator ordered the City to provide the Applicant with access to the information that it was not authorized or required to withhold under ss. 13(1) or 22(1) of FIPPA.

item.title: Metro Vancouver Regional District
item.description: Under the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act (FIPPA), an individual (applicant) asked the Metro Vancouver Regional District (Regional District) for access to information related to an investigation. The Regional District withheld records under ss. 12(3)(b) (local public body confidences) and 14 (solicitor-client privilege). The adjudicator found the Regional District was authorized to withhold all the records in dispute under s. 14.
